In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a laser pulse with an energy of several joules can be focused onto an area of ~1 mm2 and the resulting radiation can be used to ionize air to a degree sufficient for the production of a plasma with a density of 10-2 cm-3.
the interaction of a laser pulse of 10(14)-10(15) W/cm2 intensity with a target leads to a high-temperature (10(6) K), high-density (10(4) g/cm3) plasma.
the ionization of ambient air is not a significant effect in the interaction of a laser pulse of intensity ~1013 Wcm-2 with a target in the pressure range 0.1-10 Torr.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction of laser radiation with a target is characterized by the presence of a number of different physical processes, which, however, are closely related to each other.
the laser pulse is capable of ionizing the air to the extent that the plasma is optically thin to x rays.

the laser pulse energy required to produce the same degree of ionization in a given volume of air is ~10 times less when the laser pulse is focused on a target than when it is focused in a vacuum chamber.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree of ionizaton is determined by the balance of the ionization and recombination rates and is not limited by the ionization rate.
the degree of ionizaiton of air in this case reaches ~10-2, which is sufficient for the generation of a plasma channel.
the ionization of the ambient gas by x rays is the dominant mechanism of ionization in this regime.
